title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Production traffic patterns expose two related issues in the continuous-batcher scheduler: 1) unfair queueing where long-running large-sequence requests can starve short low-latency requests; 2) requests stuck in the queue past useful time windows when downstream callers have already timed out. This PR introduces a set of scheduler and policy changes to address queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and configurable queue timeouts. High level changes: 1) Add priority-agnostic aging (priority_age) to boost waiting requests over time so short requests don't get perpetually deprioritized by a stream of large requests; 2) Introduce per-request max_queue_time_ms with a default of 200ms and a per-queue fallback; requests that exceed this are evicted with a well-defined timeout error to callers and metrics; 3) Replace simple FIFO-with-buckets with a multi-tier fair-queue implementation (an adaptation of deficit round-robin tuned for small-batch fairness) to better balance throughput and latency across request sizes; 4) Add starvation detectors and a soft-eviction policy for excessive waiters on a worker (prevents head-of-line blocking caused by KV-cache warming edge-cases); 5) New observability: metrics for queue_wait_time_ms histogram, evicted_due_to_timeout, starvation_count, fairness_score (0-1) per queue and per model_route. Implementation details: - core scheduler changes in continuous_batcher/scheduler.go: added 'priority_age' bookkeeping for queued requests, updated dequeue() to prefer aged requests above a dynamic threshold, and implemented per-queue deficit counters; - queue management in continuous_batcher/queue.go: per-request metadata field max_queue_time_ms and enqueue timestamp; eviction path added to return ErrQueueTimeout; - worker loop adjustments in serving/worker_pool.go to surface eviction errors and avoid spinning when queues are empty; - configs: new scheduler tuning parameters in config/scheduler.yaml (max_queue_time_ms, aging_increment_ms, fairness_window_ms, starvation_threshold_count) with safe defaults; - tests: added unit tests under continuous_batcher/*_test.go covering aging behavior, eviction, and fairness invariants; added integration test in perf-canary that simulates a mixed workload (short chat requests + long context generation) to validate p50/p99 behavior; - docs: updated redwood-docs/docs/continuous-batching.md with guidance and tuning recommendations for Dedicated and Private deployments. Benchmarks and results: - Microbenchmarks on a 4xA100 pool with mixed workload (70% short 64-token requests, 30% long 2048-token requests) show: p50 latency for short requests improved from 22ms to 16ms; p95 improved from 78ms to 48ms; p99 incidents of starvation (requests waiting >500ms) reduced from 3.4% to 0.2%; overall throughput change within -2% of baseline (acceptable trade-off). Operational considerations and rollout: - Feature is behind runtime feature-flag continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2 (off by default in hosted), enabled in Dedicated staging for 48h Canary. - Default max_queue_time_ms=200ms can be increased per customer workloads; SDKs will surface the header X-Redwood-Max-Queue-Time for quick override. - Added migration note: no breaking API changes; evicted requests return structured error with code QUEUE_TIMEOUT. Checklist: - [x] Scheduler logic implemented and unit tested - [x] Integration/perf tests added - [x] Config and docs updated - [x] Metrics and tracing hooks added - [x] Feature gated and rollout plan documented Related: ENG-1428 tracks longer-term scheduling algorithm exploration, SUP-7891 is the customer case that motivated shorter queue timeouts.

release_notes: Scheduler: continuous-batcher scheduler tuned for queueing fairness and starvation prevention. Introduces priority aging, per-request max_queue_time_ms (default 200ms), and new metrics (queue_wait_time_ms, evicted_due_to_timeout). Enabled behind feature flag continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2. See docs for tuning guidance.
notes: Deployed to Dedicated staging and observed no regressions in throughput; recommended for gradual rollout. Customers with extremely high variance workloads can raise max_queue_time_ms per-route.
